messages:
sasha: Quick dump of a spike we saw on canary after enabling multi-variant routing for 'mix-small'. batching efficiency dropped ~18%. attaching profiler output and log excerpt.

sasha: log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z INFO route=mv-routing variant=small fallback=true batch_size=3 token_budget=120 kv_hit=false kernel=generic
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z INFO batch=2463 formed=2 target=6 compat_set_size=4
```

sasha: flame link: https://internal.perf/redwood/flame/FL12345 (shows long kernel selection stalls and repeated kv miss spikes)

jon: curious — is this mostly due to compat-set fragmentation or KV cache eviction because variants are interleaving?

sasha: both. profiler shows repeated kernel recompile/selection jitter when requests switch between quantized and non-quantized variants. that forces fallback to generic kernel for a few hundred ms, which suppresses coalescing. KV cache hit-rate drops when small-variant requests evict prefix entries used by large-variant requests.

maria: rough numbers?
jon: from the run: global batch formation rate down 22%, avg batch size 3.1 -> 2.4, kv hit-rate drop 14pp on the node serving mix-small. fallbacks accounted for ~9% of tokens served with non-opt kernel.

kevin: hypothesis: our current queue policy uses a single token-budget per-GPU that doesn't account for variant-affinity. when variants are mixed, the scheduler keeps small tokens around waiting and ends up forming many small batches.

maria: proposed quick experiment: try per-compat token buckets that prefer forming intra-compat batches for the first 40ms, then relax. this should reduce kernel churn and keep KV affinity for short-lived prefixes.

jon: +1. also cap fallback window to 120ms and try making kernel selection sticky for a single batch epoch (avoid immediate reselect).

perf-bot: scheduled experiment: per-compat-tokenbucket-40ms + kernel-sticky-120ms canary -> alloc cluster r5-12 on next deploy. test duration 1h.

sasha: thanks. I'll add a short eval harness targeting the observed traffic shape (80% small prompts, 20% long) and measure: batch size distribution, kv hit-rate, kernel fallback rate, and p95 latency.

kevin: if this shows improvement we should consider a small change to routing: prefer packing variants with shared quantization tags into the same compat_set to reduce kernel divergence. but that's a follow-up.

maria: note: watch out for starvation of low-volume variants — per-compat buckets must have an emergency drain after 200ms to avoid indefinite queuing.

jon: ack. will monitor. if canary looks good, plan a gradual rollout with telemetry alerts for kernel-fallback > 5% and kv-hit < baseline-10pp.

sasha: I'll post results here after the 1h run (perf-bot will also post). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
